parts.t: Early associations and the first stirrings
items: 1892 (to fight British rule on social issues)
Born after arrest of Annie Besant
**Mulla Abdul Qayyum:** first Muslim leader from Hyderabad to join the INC.
**Govinda Rao Nanal:** first President of the Hyderabad State Congress.
**First Telugu / Andhra President of INC:** P. Anandacharyulu (1891, Nagpur session); the first Telugu man to preside.
**First President of Andhra Congress Circle:** Nyapati Subba Rao.
**First All India Congress Session in Andhra:** Vijayawada, 1921.
**AICC session, 1906 (Dadabhai Naoroji):** Pingali Venkayya was inspired to design the national flag.
**History of Indian National Congress:** written by Dr. Pattabhi Sitaramayya (Sitaramaiah).
**Swarajya (English daily):** started by T. Prakasam on 29-10-1921 to spread the Congress message.
**Kurnool Circular:** issued by State Congress leaders during the Quit India Movement.

parts.t: Vandemataram and Swadeshi Movement in Andhra
items: **Bipin Chandra Pal:** toured the Andhra districts during the Vandemataram Movement (guest of Ramadasu Naidu at Machilipatnam).
**Bala Bharathi Samiti:** founded by the youth of Rajahmundry in February 1907 (Swadeshi Movement).
**Rajahmundry College / Training College incident (1907):** known as the beginning of student participation in the freedom struggle from AP; Principal: Mark Hunter.
**Gadicherla Harisarvothama Rao:** teacher trainee restricted from college during the Vandemataram Movement.
**First criminal case in Vandemataram Movement:** Kakinada Riot Case.
**Andhra Jatheeya Kalasala (National College), Machilipatnam:** established 1910 by Hanumanta Rao + Krishna Rao + Pattabhi; nationalist / vocational education; President: Konda Venkatappaiah.
**Home Rule Movement (Andhra):** Gadicherla Hari Sarvothama Rao; branches started under his leadership. Founder overall: Annie Besant.
**Gadicherla Hari Sarvothama Rao:** named the Ceded Districts as Rayalaseema.
Against formation of Chirala municipality; associated with Ramadandu
First started in Palnadu (Guntur), during Non-Cooperation
**Unnava Lakshminarayana:** visited the Palnadu area in July 1921 to study the Forest Satyagraha; wrote Malapalli.
**First lawyer in Andhra to boycott British courts:** Nyapati Subba Rao.
**Nationalist song “Makoddu ye tella doratanamu”:** written by Garimella Satyanarayana (during the nationalist movement).

parts.t: Alluri Sitarama Raju and the Rampa Rebellion
items: **Rampa Rebellion:** 1922–24, Andhra region; leader: Alluri Sitarama Raju.
**First police station attacked by Alluri Sitarama Raju:** Chintapalli.
**First face-to-face war (1922):** between the British army and the followers of Alluri at Panjerighat.
**Salt Satyagraha centres:** Chinnapuram (Machilipatnam), Mypadu (Nellore) and Devarampadu (Ongole).
**Madras city:** T. Prakasam and Durgabai broke the salt laws there.
**First woman arrested in Salt Satyagraha:** Vallabhaneni Sitamahalakshmi.
**Simon Commission:** Prakasam got the title “Andhra Kesari” during its boycott (after the Simon Go Back agitation).
**Mahatma Gandhi visited Hyderabad:** 9-3-1934 (March 9, 1934), for Harijan uplift work.
**Prativadi Bhayankarachari:** closely associated with the Kakinada Conspiracy Case.
**Kisan / Agrarian Movement:** N.G. Ranga led the movement in Andhra.
**First Kisan School:** Nidubrolu, started by N.G. Ranga.
**School of Politics:** at Kanikapadu (1939), N.G. Ranga.
**Anti-Zamindari Movement (Nellore):** Vennelakanti Raghavayya played an important role.
**First Secretary of Andhra unit of Socialist Party**
**Konda Venkatappayya:** Father of Andhra State Movement; Secretary of the first Andhra Mahasabha.
**Krishna Patrika:** editor Mutnuri Krishna Rao; Konda Venkatappayya was also one of the founders and the first editor.
**Andhra Pradesh Gandhiji:** book by Vavilala Gopalakrishnayya.

parts.t: The revolutionary movement and its personalities
items: **Revolutionary Movement – important personalities:** Bhagat Singh, Chandrashekhar Azad, Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan, Surya Sen, Aurobindo Ghosh.

parts.t: Aurobindo Ghosh and the Maniktalla case
items: **1908:** Aurobindo Ghosh was arrested during the Maniktalla Garden raid.
**Maniktalla case:** held in jail for one year as an undertrial; acquitted and released for lack of evidence.

parts.t: The Ghadar Party and its journal
items: **Ghadar Party:** 1913; Lala Har Dayal (Hardayal) and Sohan Singh Bhakna.
**Ghadar:** revolutionary journal of the Ghadar Party; Lala Hardayal, Sohan Singh Bhakna and Kartar Singh Sarabha are associated with it (Ghadar movement).

corrections.title: Freedom Movement in Andhra
corrections.corrected: Chirala-Perala Movement: against formation of Chirala municipality; associated with Ramadandu
corrections.checked: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya's volunteer corps in the Chirala-Perala struggle was named Ramadandu; 'Ramanandu' is a garbled name (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duggirala_Gopalakrishnayya; https://thehansindia.com/life-style/chirala-perala-movement-was-led-by-the-pride-of-andhra-duggirala-gopalakrishnayya-815807).

corrections.title: Freedom Movement in Andhra
corrections.rocket: Swarajya (English daily) - Started by T. Prakasam on 26-10-1921 to spread Congress message
corrections.corrected: Swarajya (English daily): started by T. Prakasam on 29-10-1921 to spread the Congress message.
corrections.checked: Accounts of Prakasam's Swarajya give 29 October 1921 as the launch date; none found for 26 October (https://indianliberals.in/musings/tanguturi-prakasam-panthulu-a-visionary-leader-and-pioneer-of-press-freedom/; https://primepost.in/?p=13565).

corrections.title: Freedom Movement in Andhra
corrections.rocket: #1: First woman arrested in Salt Satyagraha - Vallabhaneni Sitamahalakshmi; #41: First woman arrested during Salt Satyagraha - Vallabhaneni Sitamahalarami
corrections.corrected: First woman arrested in Salt Satyagraha: Vallabhaneni Sitamahalakshmi.
corrections.checked: Two spellings of one name. Two web searches found no source naming her, so not web-confirmed; #1's 'Sitamahalakshmi' is a regular Telugu name and #41's 'Sitamahalarami' reads as a garble of it, so #1's spelling is kept.

corrections.title: Revolutionaries in India
corrections.rocket: Maniktalla case - Sentenced to one year; later released for lack of evidence
corrections.corrected: Maniktalla case: held in jail for one year as an undertrial; acquitted and released for lack of evidence.
corrections.checked: Aurobindo Ghosh was arrested on 2 May 1908, spent a year in Alipore jail as an undertrial and was acquitted on 6 May 1909; he was never sentenced (https://vajiramandravi.com/upsc-exam/alipore-conspiracy-case/; https://www.gktoday.in/alipore-conspiracy-case/).

corrections.title: Freedom Movement in Andhra
corrections.rocket: Alluri Sitarama Raju - Rampa Rebellion; ... Tribe: Khonds
corrections.checked: Web sources name the Koya and Konda Reddi (Konda Dora) tribes of the Godavari agency as Alluri's followers (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rampa_Rebellion_of_1922; https://www.gktoday.in/rampa-rebellion-in-andhra-region/); Khonds also live in the agency tracts, so not decisive and Rocket's line is kept.
